rationale: This sample is a tiny (791 text bytes, 2-function) FP-arithmetic benchmark whose entire body is one extremely hot, tight floating-point loop, so static data-flow obfuscation is favored over control-flow transforms that tax every iteration: FLA gets the highest SecurityGain (it most strongly resists static recovery of the loop structure) but a high RuntimeCost weight so the selector applies it selectively rather than to the whole hot path, and BCF is similarly security-valuable but penalized hard on RuntimeCost and SizeCost because bogus predicates inside a nanosecond-scale FP loop multiply into large measurable slowdown and text bloat. SUB is cheap and boosts DiversityGain substantially on arithmetic-dense code, but carries the highest CorrectnessRisk here since FP-adjacent substitutions can perturb floating-point semantics, so risk is weighted visibly. SPLIT is a low-cost enabler that improves the effectiveness of FLA/IBR with minimal runtime or size impact. IBR earns a mid weight as a good security-per-cost trade for hiding branch targets, while ICALL and IGV are near-disabled: with only main/_start and essentially no globals or indirect-call opportunities, they offer little surface to protect and would add overhead for negligible gain. Overall the table pushes the selector toward SUB+SPLIT everywhere, FLA on the main loop, and restrained BCF/IBR, keeping runtime and size acceptable for a compute benchmark while maximizing resistance to static reverse engineering.
